sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: Find the area of the region enclosed between $y=\sin x$ and $y=\cos x$ for $\pi/4\leq x\leq5\pi/4$ (the interval on which $\sin x\geq\cos x$).
questions.target: Finding the area between two curves using integration
questions.answer: Area $=\int_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4}(\sin x-\cos x)\,dx=[-\cos x-\sin x]_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4}$. At $x=5\pi/4$: $-\cos5\pi/4-\sin5\pi/4=\sqrt{2}/2+\sqrt{2}/2=\sqrt{2}$. At $x=\pi/4$: $-\cos\pi/4-\sin\pi/4=-\sqrt{2}/2-\sqrt{2}/2=-\sqrt{2}$. Area $=\sqrt{2}-(-\sqrt{2})=2\sqrt{2}$.
questions.explanation: Area $=\int_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4}(\sin x-\cos x)\,dx=[-\cos x-\sin x]_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4}$. At $x=5\pi/4$: $-\cos5\pi/4-\sin5\pi/4=\sqrt{2}/2+\sqrt{2}/2=\sqrt{2}$. At $x=\pi/4$: $-\cos\pi/4-\sin\pi/4=-\sqrt{2}/2-\sqrt{2}/2=-\sqrt{2}$. Area $=\sqrt{2}-(-\sqrt{2})=2\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int 2x(x^2+1)^4\,dx$ using the substitution $u=x^2+1$.
Evaluate $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^3x\cos x\,dx$ using the substitution $u=\sin x$.
Evaluate $\int x e^x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=e^x\,dx$, so $du=dx$, $v=e^x$. $\int xe^x\,dx=xe^x-\int e^x\,dx=xe^x-e^x+C=(x-1)e^x+C$.
questions.explanation: Let $u=x$, $dv=e^x\,dx$, so $du=dx$, $v=e^x$. $\int xe^x\,dx=xe^x-\int e^x\,dx=xe^x-e^x+C=(x-1)e^x+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x\,dx$, so $du=(1/x)\,dx$, $v=x^2/2$. $\int x\ln x\,dx=x^2/2\ln x-\int x^2/2\cdot1/x\,dx=x^2/2\ln x-x^2/4+C$.
questions.explanation: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x\,dx$, so $du=(1/x)\,dx$, $v=x^2/2$. $\int x\ln x\,dx=x^2/2\ln x-\int x^2/2\cdot1/x\,dx=x^2/2\ln x-x^2/4+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2e^x\,dx$, applying integration by parts twice.
questions.answer: First application: $u=x^2$, $dv=e^xdx$: $\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-\int2xe^x\,dx$. From the previous problem, $\int xe^x\,dx=(x-1)e^x+C$, so $\int2xe^x\,dx=2(x-1)e^x$. Result: $x^2e^x-2(x-1)e^x+C=(x^2-2x+2)e^x+C$.
questions.explanation: First application: $u=x^2$, $dv=e^xdx$: $\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-\int2xe^x\,dx$. From the previous problem, $\int xe^x\,dx=(x-1)e^x+C$, so $\int2xe^x\,dx=2(x-1)e^x$. Result: $x^2e^x-2(x-1)e^x+C=(x^2-2x+2)e^x+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\cos^2x\,dx$ using the identity $\cos^2x=(1+\cos2x)/2$.

sections.heading: Part II — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Multi-Step Application (8–14)

questions.q: Evaluate $\int1/(x^2-1)\,dx$ by first expressing the integrand in partial fractions.
Evaluate $\int_1^e\ln x/x\,dx$, using the substitution $u=\ln x$.
Evaluate $\int_0^{\pi}x\sin x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=\sin x\,dx$, so $du=dx$, $v=-\cos x$. $\int x\sin x\,dx=-x\cos x+\int\cos x\,dx=-x\cos x+\sin x$. Evaluating from $0$ to $\pi$: $[-\pi\cos\pi+\sin\pi]-[0+0]=-\pi(-1)+0=\pi$.
questions.explanation: Let $u=x$, $dv=\sin x\,dx$, so $du=dx$, $v=-\cos x$. $\int x\sin x\,dx=-x\cos x+\int\cos x\,dx=-x\cos x+\sin x$. Evaluating from $0$ to $\pi$: $[-\pi\cos\pi+\sin\pi]-[0+0]=-\pi(-1)+0=\pi$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int1/(1+x^2)\,dx$, and use it to evaluate $\int_0^1 1/(1+x^2)\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\int1/(1+x^2)\,dx=\arctan x+C$. So $\int_0^1 1/(1+x^2)\,dx=\arctan(1)-\arctan(0)=\pi/4-0=\pi/4$.
questions.explanation: $\int1/(1+x^2)\,dx=\arctan x+C$. So $\int_0^1 1/(1+x^2)\,dx=\arctan(1)-\arctan(0)=\pi/4-0=\pi/4$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\sin^3x\,dx$, using the identity $\sin^2x=1-\cos^2x$ and the substitution $u=\cos x$.
questions.target: Integration by substitution with trigonometric functions
questions.answer: Rewrite: $\sin^3x=\sin x(1-\cos^2x)$. Let $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$. $\int\sin x(1-\cos^2x)\,dx=-\int(1-u^2)\,du=-u+u^3/3+C=-\cos x+\cos^3x/3+C$.
questions.explanation: Rewrite: $\sin^3x=\sin x(1-\cos^2x)$. Let $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$. $\int\sin x(1-\cos^2x)\,dx=-\int(1-u^2)\,du=-u+u^3/3+C=-\cos x+\cos^3x/3+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\tan x\,dx$, using the substitution $u=\cos x$.
questions.target: Integration by substitution with trigonometric functions
questions.answer: $\tan x=\sin x/(\cos x)$. Let $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$. $\int\sin x/(\cos x)\,dx=-\int1/u\,du=-\ln|u|+C=-\ln|\cos x|+C=\ln|\sec x|+C$.
questions.explanation: $\tan x=\sin x/(\cos x)$. Let $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$. $\int\sin x/(\cos x)\,dx=-\int1/u\,du=-\ln|u|+C=-\ln|\cos x|+C=\ln|\sec x|+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_1^e\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.target: Integration by parts with a logarithmic integrand
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=dx$, so $du=(1/x)\,dx$, $v=x$. $\int\ln x\,dx=x\ln x-\int x\cdot1/x\,dx=x\ln x-x+C$. Evaluating from $1$ to $e$: $[e\ln e-e]-[1\ln1-1]=(e-e)-(0-1)=0+1=1$.
questions.explanation: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=dx$, so $du=(1/x)\,dx$, $v=x$. $\int\ln x\,dx=x\ln x-\int x\cdot1/x\,dx=x\ln x-x+C$. Evaluating from $1$ to $e$: $[e\ln e-e]-[1\ln1-1]=(e-e)-(0-1)=0+1=1$.

sections.heading: Part III — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: Evaluate $\int1/(5+4\cos x)\,dx$ using the substitution $t=\tan(x/2)$, given that this substitution transforms $\cos x=(1-t^2)/(1+t^2)$ and $dx=2/(1+t^2)dt$, leading to the simplified integrand $2/(9+t^2)$.
questions.cross_lesson: 3.03 Compound Angle Identities & Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions (AA HL)
questions.answer: Substituting: $\int1/(5+4(1-t^2)/(1+t^2))\cdot2/(1+t^2)\,dt=\int2/(5(1+t^2)+4(1-t^2))\,dt=\int2/(9+t^2)\,dt$. Using the standard result $\int1/(a^2+t^2)\,dt=(1/a)\arctan(t/a)+C$ with $a=3$: $2\cdot(1/3)\arctan(t/3)+C=(2/3)\arctan((1/3)\tan(x/2))+C$.
questions.explanation: Substituting: $\int1/(5+4(1-t^2)/(1+t^2))\cdot2/(1+t^2)\,dt=\int2/(5(1+t^2)+4(1-t^2))\,dt=\int2/(9+t^2)\,dt$. Using the standard result $\int1/(a^2+t^2)\,dt=(1/a)\arctan(t/a)+C$ with $a=3$: $2\cdot(1/3)\arctan(t/3)+C=(2/3)\arctan((1/3)\tan(x/2))+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int e^x\cos x\,dx$, applying integration by parts twice and solving the resulting equation for the original integral.
questions.target: Integration by parts with a trigonometric-exponential product
questions.answer: Let $I=\int e^x\cos x\,dx$. First application: $u=\cos x$, $dv=e^xdx$, so $du=-\sin x\,dx$, $v=e^x$: $I=e^x\cos x+\int e^x\sin x\,dx$. Second application on $\int e^x\sin x\,dx$: $u=\sin x$, $dv=e^xdx$: $\int e^x\sin x\,dx=e^x\sin x-\int e^x\cos x\,dx=e^x\sin x-I$. Substituting back: $I=e^x\cos x+e^x\sin x-I$, so $2I=e^x(\cos x+\sin x)$, giving $I=e^x(\cos x+\sin x)/2+C$.
questions.explanation: Let $I=\int e^x\cos x\,dx$. First application: $u=\cos x$, $dv=e^xdx$, so $du=-\sin x\,dx$, $v=e^x$: $I=e^x\cos x+\int e^x\sin x\,dx$. Second application on $\int e^x\sin x\,dx$: $u=\sin x$, $dv=e^xdx$: $\int e^x\sin x\,dx=e^x\sin x-\int e^x\cos x\,dx=e^x\sin x-I$. Substituting back: $I=e^x\cos x+e^x\sin x-I$, so $2I=e^x(\cos x+\sin x)$, giving $I=e^x(\cos x+\sin x)/2+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.target: Finding the area between two curves using integration
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x^2dx$, so $du=(1/x)\,dx$, $v=x^3/3$. $\int x^2\ln x\,dx=x^3/3\ln x-\int x^3/3\cdot1/x\,dx=x^3/3\ln x-\int x^2/3\,dx=x^3/3\ln x-x^3/9+C$.
questions.explanation: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x^2dx$, so $du=(1/x)\,dx$, $v=x^3/3$. $\int x^2\ln x\,dx=x^3/3\ln x-\int x^3/3\cdot1/x\,dx=x^3/3\ln x-\int x^2/3\,dx=x^3/3\ln x-x^3/9+C$.

questions.q: A particle's velocity is given by $v(t)=t\cos t$ metres per second. Find the particle's displacement over the interval $0\leq t\leq\pi$, using integration by parts.
questions.target: Finding the area between two curves using integration
questions.answer: Displacement $=\int_0^{\pi}t\cos t\,dt$. Using integration by parts with $u=t$, $dv=\cos t\,dt$, so $du=dt$, $v=\sin t$: $\int t\cos t\,dt=t\sin t-\int\sin t\,dt=t\sin t+\cos t+C$. Evaluating from $0$ to $\pi$: $[\pi\sin\pi+\cos\pi]-[0\sin0+\cos0]=[0-1]-[0+1]=-1-1=-2$. Displacement $=-2$ metres.
questions.explanation: Displacement $=\int_0^{\pi}t\cos t\,dt$. Using integration by parts with $u=t$, $dv=\cos t\,dt$, so $du=dt$, $v=\sin t$: $\int t\cos t\,dt=t\sin t-\int\sin t\,dt=t\sin t+\cos t+C$. Evaluating from $0$ to $\pi$: $[\pi\sin\pi+\cos\pi]-[0\sin0+\cos0]=[0-1]-[0+1]=-1-1=-2$. Displacement $=-2$ metres.

questions.q: This question has three parts. (a) Use the substitution $u=x^2+4$ to find $\int x/(x^2+4)\,dx$. (b) Use integration by parts to find $\int\arctan x\,dx$. (c) Hence, using the result of part (b) and the standard result $\int1/(1+x^2)dx=\arctan x+C$, evaluate $\int_0^1\arctan x\,dx$, giving an exact answer in terms of $\pi$ and $\ln$.
questions.target: Finding the area between two curves using integration
questions.answer: (a) $u=x^2+4$, $du=2x\,dx$: $\int x/(x^2+4)\,dx=1/2\int1/u\,du=1/2\ln|x^2+4|+C$. (b) Let $u=\arctan x$, $dv=dx$, so $du=(1/(1+x^2))\,dx$, $v=x$: $\int\arctan x\,dx=x\arctan x-\int x/(1+x^2)\,dx=x\arctan x-1/2\ln(1+x^2)+C$ (using the result from part (a), with $4$ replaced by $1$). (c) Evaluating from $0$ to $1$: $[1\cdot\arctan1-1/2\ln2]-[0-1/2\ln1]=\pi/4-1/2\ln2$.
questions.explanation: (a) $u=x^2+4$, $du=2x\,dx$: $\int x/(x^2+4)\,dx=1/2\int1/u\,du=1/2\ln|x^2+4|+C$. (b) Let $u=\arctan x$, $dv=dx$, so $du=(1/(1+x^2))\,dx$, $v=x$: $\int\arctan x\,dx=x\arctan x-\int x/(1+x^2)\,dx=x\arctan x-1/2\ln(1+x^2)+C$ (using the result from part (a), with $4$ replaced by $1$). (c) Evaluating from $0$ to $1$: $[1\cdot\arctan1-1/2\ln2]-[0-1/2\ln1]=\pi/4-1/2\ln2$.

questions.q: Given the reduction formula $I_n=\int x^ne^x\,dx=x^ne^x-nI_{n-1}$ (obtained via integration by parts), and that $I_0=e^x+C$, use it to find $I_2=\int x^2e^x\,dx$.
questions.cross_lesson: 5.04 Graphs of Inverse Trigonometric Functions & Their Derivatives (AA HL)
questions.answer: $I_1=x^1e^x-1\cdot I_0=xe^x-e^x$ (ignoring the constant until the final step). $I_2=x^2e^x-2I_1=x^2e^x-2(xe^x-e^x)=x^2e^x-2xe^x+2e^x+C=(x^2-2x+2)e^x+C$, matching the result found earlier in this worksheet by direct repeated integration by parts.
questions.explanation: $I_1=x^1e^x-1\cdot I_0=xe^x-e^x$ (ignoring the constant until the final step). $I_2=x^2e^x-2I_1=x^2e^x-2(xe^x-e^x)=x^2e^x-2xe^x+2e^x+C=(x^2-2x+2)e^x+C$, matching the result found earlier in this worksheet by direct repeated integration by parts.

sections.heading: Part IV — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Concept Mastery (21–28)

questions.q: Which integration technique is most appropriate for evaluating $\int x^3\sin x\,dx$?
choices: Integration by parts, applied three times (reducing the power of $x$ each time)
questions.answer: Since the integrand is a product of a polynomial and a trigonometric function, integration by parts is appropriate — and because the polynomial factor is $x^3$ (not $x^1$), the process must be repeated three times, each time reducing the power of $x$ by one, until the polynomial factor disappears.
questions.explanation: Since the integrand is a product of a polynomial and a trigonometric function, integration by parts is appropriate — and because the polynomial factor is $x^3$ (not $x^1$), the process must be repeated three times, each time reducing the power of $x$ by one, until the polynomial factor disappears.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2 \cos x dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Tabular: $x^2 \rightarrow 2x \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 0$; $\cos x \rightarrow \sin x \rightarrow -\cos x \rightarrow -\sin x$. Alternating: $+x^2\sin x - 2x(-\cos x) + 2(-\sin x) = x^2\sin x + 2x\cos x - 2\sin x + C$.
questions.explanation: Tabular: $x^2 \rightarrow 2x \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 0$; $\cos x \rightarrow \sin x \rightarrow -\cos x \rightarrow -\sin x$. Alternating: $+x^2\sin x - 2x(-\cos x) + 2(-\sin x) = x^2\sin x + 2x\cos x - 2\sin x + C$.

questions.q: Evaluate the cyclic integral $I = \int e^x \sin x dx$.
questions.answer: Integrate by parts twice: $I = e^x \sin x - \int e^x \cos x dx = e^x \sin x - [e^x \cos x - \int e^x (-\sin x)dx] = e^x(\sin x - \cos x) - I \Rightarrow 2I = e^x(\sin x - \cos x) \Rightarrow I = \frac{1}{2}e^x(\sin x - \cos x) + C$.
questions.explanation: Integrate by parts twice: $I = e^x \sin x - \int e^x \cos x dx = e^x \sin x - [e^x \cos x - \int e^x (-\sin x)dx] = e^x(\sin x - \cos x) - I \Rightarrow 2I = e^x(\sin x - \cos x) \Rightarrow I = \frac{1}{2}e^x(\sin x - \cos x) + C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_1^e \ln x dx$.
questions.answer: $\int \ln x dx = x\ln x - x$. Evaluating from 1 to $e$: $[e\ln e - e] - [1\ln 1 - 1] = [e - e] - [0 - 1] = 0 - (-1) = 1$.
questions.explanation: $\int \ln x dx = x\ln x - x$. Evaluating from 1 to $e$: $[e\ln e - e] - [1\ln 1 - 1] = [e - e] - [0 - 1] = 0 - (-1) = 1$.

questions.q: Which trigonometric substitution is best suited to evaluate $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{16 - x^2}} dx$?
questions.answer: For forms $\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}$, the substitution $x = a\sin\theta$ simplifies the radical via $16 - 16\sin^2\theta = 16\cos^2\theta$.
questions.explanation: For forms $\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}$, the substitution $x = a\sin\theta$ simplifies the radical via $16 - 16\sin^2\theta = 16\cos^2\theta$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int \frac{1}{x^2 + 16} dx$.
questions.answer: Standard formula $\int \frac{1}{x^2 + a^2} dx = \frac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\frac{x}{a}\right) + C$. With $a = 4$: $\frac{1}{4}\arctan\left(\frac{x}{4}\right) + C$.
questions.explanation: Standard formula $\int \frac{1}{x^2 + a^2} dx = \frac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\frac{x}{a}\right) + C$. With $a = 4$: $\frac{1}{4}\arctan\left(\frac{x}{4}\right) + C$.

questions.q: Which substitution evaluates $\int \sqrt{x^2 - 9} dx$?
questions.answer: For $\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}$, use $x = a\sec\theta$, since $x^2 - 9 = 9(\sec^2\theta - 1) = 9\tan^2\theta$.
questions.explanation: For $\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}$, use $x = a\sec\theta$, since $x^2 - 9 = 9(\sec^2\theta - 1) = 9\tan^2\theta$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int \sin^3 x dx$.
questions.target: Integrals of Powers of Trigonometric Functions
questions.answer: Rewrite $\sin^3 x = (1 - \cos^2 x)\sin x$. Let $u = \cos x, du = -\sin x dx$: $\int -(1 - u^2) du = -u + \frac{u^3}{3} + C = -\cos x + \frac{1}{3}\cos^3 x + C$.
questions.explanation: Rewrite $\sin^3 x = (1 - \cos^2 x)\sin x$. Let $u = \cos x, du = -\sin x dx$: $\int -(1 - u^2) du = -u + \frac{u^3}{3} + C = -\cos x + \frac{1}{3}\cos^3 x + C$.

sections.heading: Part V — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Exam Application (29–37)

questions.q: Evaluate $\int \cos^2 x dx$.
questions.target: Integrals of Powers of Trigonometric Functions
questions.answer: Use double angle identity $\cos^2 x = \frac{1 + \cos(2x)}{2}$: $\int \frac{1 + \cos(2x)}{2} dx = \frac{x}{2} + \frac{\sin(2x)}{4} + C$.
questions.explanation: Use double angle identity $\cos^2 x = \frac{1 + \cos(2x)}{2}$: $\int \frac{1 + \cos(2x)}{2} dx = \frac{x}{2} + \frac{\sin(2x)}{4} + C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int \tan^2 x dx$.
questions.target: Integrals of Powers of Trigonometric Functions
questions.answer: Identity: $\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1$. Integrating: $\int (\sec^2 x - 1) dx = \tan x - x + C$.
questions.explanation: Identity: $\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1$. Integrating: $\int (\sec^2 x - 1) dx = \tan x - x + C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int \frac{x}{\sqrt{x + 1}} dx$ using substitution $u = x + 1$.
Evaluate $\int_0^1 \frac{e^x}{1 + e^x} dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u = 1 + e^x, du = e^x dx$. At $x = 0, u = 2$; at $x = 1, u = 1 + e$. $\int_2^{1+e} \frac{1}{u} du = [\ln|u|]_2^{1+e} = \ln(1 + e) - \ln 2 = \ln\left(\frac{1 + e}{2}\right)$.
questions.explanation: Let $u = 1 + e^x, du = e^x dx$. At $x = 0, u = 2$; at $x = 1, u = 1 + e$. $\int_2^{1+e} \frac{1}{u} du = [\ln|u|]_2^{1+e} = \ln(1 + e) - \ln 2 = \ln\left(\frac{1 + e}{2}\right)$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int \frac{1}{x\ln x} dx$ for $x > 1$.
questions.answer: Let $u = \ln x, du = \frac{1}{x}dx$. $\int \frac{1}{u} du = \ln|u| + C = \ln|\ln x| + C$.
questions.explanation: Let $u = \ln x, du = \frac{1}{x}dx$. $\int \frac{1}{u} du = \ln|u| + C = \ln|\ln x| + C$.

questions.q: Consider the function $f(x) = \frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(x)}$. For the domain $x \in [0, 2\pi]$ such that $\cos(x) eq 0$, find the exact value of the definite integral $\int_{0}^{\pi/2} f(x) dx$.
questions.target: Integration by substitution with a linear inner function
questions.answer: First, we simplify the function $f(x)$. Using the double angle identity for sine, $\sin(2x) = 2\sin(x)\cos(x)$. Therefore, $f(x) = \frac{2\sin(x)\cos(x)}{\cos(x)}$. For $\cos(x) eq 0$, we can cancel the $\cos(x)$ terms, so $f(x) = 2\sin(x)$. Now we need to evaluate the definite integral: $\int_{0}^{\pi/2} 2\sin(x) dx$. The antiderivative of $2\sin(x)$ is $-2\cos(x)$. Evaluating the definite integral using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: $[-2\cos(x)]_{0}^{\pi/2} = -2\cos(\pi/2) - (-2\cos(0))$ $= -2(0) - (-2(1))$ $= 0 - (-2)$ $= 2$ Thus, the exact value of the definite integral is 2.
questions.explanation: First, we simplify the function $f(x)$. Using the double angle identity for sine, $\sin(2x) = 2\sin(x)\cos(x)$. Therefore, $f(x) = \frac{2\sin(x)\cos(x)}{\cos(x)}$. For $\cos(x) eq 0$, we can cancel the $\cos(x)$ terms, so $f(x) = 2\sin(x)$. Now we need to evaluate the definite integral: $\int_{0}^{\pi/2} 2\sin(x) dx$. The antiderivative of $2\sin(x)$ is $-2\cos(x)$. Evaluating the definite integral using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: $[-2\cos(x)]_{0}^{\pi/2} = -2\cos(\pi/2) - (-2\cos(0))$ $= -2(0) - (-2(1))$ $= 0 - (-2)$ $= 2$ Thus, the exact value of the definite integral is 2.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\frac{7}{x}$ (a self-inverse function), find the positive value of $x$ for which $f(x)=x$ (a fixed point).
questions.target: Integration using the sine double-angle identity
questions.answer: $\frac{7}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=7 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{7}$
questions.explanation: $\frac{7}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=7 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{7}$

questions.q: If $f(x)=\frac{8}{x}$ (a self-inverse function), find the positive value of $x$ for which $f(x)=x$ (a fixed point).
questions.answer: $\frac{8}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=8 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{8}$
questions.explanation: $\frac{8}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=8 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{8}$

questions.q: If $f(x)=\frac{5}{x}$ (a self-inverse function), find the positive value of $x$ for which $f(x)=x$ (a fixed point).
questions.target: Substitution with a shifting definite integral bound
questions.answer: $\frac{5}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=5 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{5}$
questions.explanation: $\frac{5}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=5 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{5}$

questions.q: If $f(x)=\frac{3}{x}$ (a self-inverse function), find the positive value of $x$ for which $f(x)=x$ (a fixed point).
questions.answer: $\frac{3}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=3 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{3}$
questions.explanation: $\frac{3}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=3 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{3}$

questions.q: If $f(x)=\frac{4}{x}$ (a self-inverse function), find the positive value of $x$ for which $f(x)=x$ (a fixed point).
questions.answer: $\frac{4}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=4 \Rightarrow x=2$
questions.explanation: $\frac{4}{x}=x \Rightarrow x^2=4 \Rightarrow x=2$

questions.q: Find the angle between lines with direction vectors $\mathbf{d_1}=\left(1 ; 4 ; 8\right)$ and $\mathbf{d_2}=\left(4 ; -1 ; 0\right)$.
questions.target: Integrals of Powers of Trigonometric Functions
questions.answer: $\mathbf{d_1}\cdot\mathbf{d_2}=0=0 \Rightarrow \theta=90^\circ$
questions.explanation: $\mathbf{d_1}\cdot\mathbf{d_2}=0=0 \Rightarrow \theta=90^\circ$
